title: OWASP Top 10 for Web & LLM Applications
description: Analyze the OWASP Top 10 for web applications alongside the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, with defensive engineering controls in C#.

data.text: The Convergence of Web and AI Security

While traditional web security defends against SQL injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and Broken Access Control (OWASP Top 10 Web), generative AI introduces an entirely separate risk profile. The OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications codifies the critical vulnerabilities that arise when natural language models interact with software systems, data stores, and external APIs.
The OWASP Top 10 for LLMs Explained

rows: LLM01: Prompt Injection
Manipulating prompts via direct user input or indirect retrieved documents
Hijacks model instructions, bypasses safety guardrails
Strict XML context boundaries, Azure Content Safety Prompt Shields
LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure
Model reveals PII, API credentials, or proprietary source data in completions
Data privacy violations, regulatory fines (GDPR/HIPAA)
PII masking middleware (Presidio), outbound DLP screening
LLM03: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
Compromised third-party models, poisoned plugins, or vulnerable packages
Backdoored model weights, malware execution
Scan NuGet packages with dotnet list package --vulnerable; verify model signatures
LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning
Tampering with training data or RAG knowledge bases
Corrupts model decision-making or creates deliberate backdoor triggers
Cryptographic document hashing, verified source ingestion pipelines
LLM05: Improper Output Handling
Passing raw LLM outputs to downstream interpreters (eval(), bash, SQL, innerHTML)
Remote Code Execution (RCE), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Strict JSON schema validation; HTML entity encoding; parameterized SQL
LLM06: Excessive Agency
Granting autonomous agents unrestricted access to high-privilege tools
Accidental mass deletion, unintended financial transactions
Least privilege tool roles, rate limits, Human-in-the-Loop confirmation tokens
LLM07: System Prompt Leakage
Tricking the model into disclosing proprietary internal instructions
Intellectual property theft, reveals internal API structures
Negative system prompt constraints, anti-leakage filters
LLM08: Vector & Embedding Weaknesses
Injecting poisoned vectors into shared stores to manipulate RAG retrieval
Skewed search results, retrieval of malicious external text
Strict tenant partitioning, sanitize embeddings before storage

data.text: Mitigating Improper Output Handling in C#
Never pass raw model outputs directly into database queries, command-line processes, or React innerHTML. Always treat model output as untrusted user input.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Enterprise security requires mastering both the OWASP Web Top 10 and the OWASP LLM Top 10
LLM01 (Prompt Injection) and LLM06 (Excessive Agency) represent the highest operational risks to agents
Never treat LLM output as trusted: validate against schemas before database or API execution
Implement Human-in-the-Loop verification tokens to counter Excessive Agency on mutating actions
Audit NuGet dependencies and container images for supply chain vulnerabilities
data.takeaway: The OWASP LLM Top 10 provides the architectural blueprint for hardening generative AI applications. Applying defense-in-depth across prompts, models, and tools prevents catastrophic security failures.
